questions.question: Which two URLs have different origins?
questions.explanation: An origin is scheme plus host plus port, so adding a port creates a different origin.

questions.question: Who enforces the CORS rules?
questions.explanation: Browsers check the allow headers and block the page from reading the reply. Servers only send the headers.

questions.question: The API allows only http://localhost:3000. A request arrives with Origin: http://evil.example.com. What does Spring MVC reply?
options: 200 with the data and no allow header
403 with the text Invalid CORS request
questions.explanation: The origin is not on the list, so Spring rejects the CORS request with 403.

questions.question: Which header in a preflight reply tells the browser it may cache the answer for an hour?
questions.explanation: maxAge(3600) produces Access-Control-Max-Age: 3600, so the browser can skip the preflight for one hour.

questions.question: A config uses allowedOrigins("*") together with allowCredentials(true). What is the problem?
options: Nothing, it is the recommended setup
It works only for GET requests
Spring rejects the combination, because cookies need exact origins
questions.explanation: A wildcard origin cannot be combined with allowCredentials(true), so list the real origins instead.
